Mahud Ali and Others
Vs.

full_judgment: 15. Conviction and sentence passed on the appellants and Kitab Ali is, therefore illegal and cannot be sustained. We must therefore, set aside the conviction and sentence of the appellants before us and, exercising suo moto power under section 439 Cr.P.C. also the conviction and sentence of Kitab Ali who has not appealed. This Court is not only competent to set aside the conviction and sentence of Kitab Ali but it is also imperative upon this court to do so in view of its finding that the conviction of Kitab Ali is illegal. The view that we were taking has also been taken in a number of previous decisions. In Reference No.61 of 1950 reported in 2 D.L.R. 305, a Division Bench the Dhaka High Court, on a reference made by a Sessions Judge under section 438 Cr.P.C. against the conviction of one accused suo motto set aside the conviction and sentence of another accused who was also convicted, on the ground of the conviction being illegal though this another accused did not move the High Court against his conviction. In the case of Abdul Hafez Sarder V. The State reported in 28 D.L.R.253, a single judge of this Court took the view that the High Court can under section 439 Cr.P.C. suo moto take cognizance of the case of an accused who has not appealed and set aside his conviction and sentence which has been found to be illegal. In the cases of Zamir Hossain and others V. The Crown reported in P.L.D. 1949 Lahore 179 and Raza Muhammad and others V. The State reported in P.L.D. 1965 (W.P.) Karachi 637, a similar view was taken and conviction and sentence of non-appealing accused, set aside.
